content.title: Main Card Results | UFC Seattle
content.text: There is something about Seattle that brings out electric performances as for the second consecutive year, the Octagon was alight with action at Climate Pledge Arena on Saturday night. Following a captivating slate of preliminary card bouts, business picked up on the main card with a series of stunning of finishes, including a fairytale ending for Michael Chiesa, before Joe Pyfer wrapped things up by earning the biggest win of his career. If you missed any of the action, check out our recaps below. UFC Fight Night: Adesanya vs Pyfer took place Saturday, March 28, live from Climate Pledge Arena in Seattle, Washington. The prelims began at 5pm ET/2pm PT, followed by the main card at 8pm ET/5pm PT. The entire event can be relived on Paramount+. Watch Every UFC Event On Paramount+ Results, Highlights & Backstage Interviews Joe Pyfer defeated Israel Adesanya by TKO (strikes) at 4:18 of Round 2 Joe Pyfer earned the biggest win of his career on Saturday night, stopping former middleweight champion Israel Adesanya in the second round. The two men opted to go toe-to-toe in the second round, putting their defenses aside in order to trade blows in the pocket, accepting that someone was going to catch something sharp. Alexa Grasso Finishes Maycee Barber In The First | UFC Seattle As the two engaged in space, Grasso connected with a left hand in the heat of an exchange that twisted Barber around awkwardly. As she began to collapse to the canvas, Grasso quickly latched onto a rear-naked choke out of instinct but was not needed; Barber was out and Grasso was back in the win column. Michael Chiesa Post-Fight Interview | UFC Seattle This was the fairytale ending to a storybook career for the 38-year-old from Spokane, Washington, who hung up his gloves on Saturday night, retiring on a four-fight winning streak. The Ultimate Fighter: Live winner retired with a 20-7 record overall, including a 15-7 mark inside the Octagon. | Prelim Results | Official Scorecards Lerryan Douglas defeated Julian Erosa by KO (strikes) at 3:33 of Round 1 Lerryan Douglas authored one of the best promotional debuts of the year, stopping Julian Erosa in the first round. From the outset, the power of the Brazilian was too much for Erosa to deal with, starting with the calf kicks and building to the hands, where the recent Dana White’s Contender Series grab was rocking the Washington state product with stiff jabs. Lerryan Douglas Post-Fight Interview | UFC Seattle With Erosa clearly in a bad way, Douglas continued to pour it on, finally ending thigs along the fence. This was a dangerous debut assignment and Douglas handled it with aplomb, blowing through Erosa to collect his sixth straight win. The Brazilian “Gunslinger” is older and more seasoned than most newcomers and showed on Saturday that he’s an instant threat in the 145-pound weight class. | Prelim Results | Official Scorecards Yousri Belgaroui defeated Mansur Abdul-Malik by KO (knee) at 3:39 of Round 3 Yousri Belgaroui knocked off another talented middleweight prospect on Saturday, following up his debut win with a dominant third-round finish of Mansur Abdul-Malik.
